name: Nucleoid (Chromosomal DNA)
description: The irregularly shaped region within the cell where the ~4.6 million base pair circular chromosome is localized. UV radiation causes thymine dimers and double-strand breaks along this DNA.

name: Ribosomes
description: Complex molecular machines (70S in bacteria) that translate mRNA into proteins. During the SOS response, ribosomes translate upregulated repair genes.

name: GamGFP (DSB Sensor)
description: A fusion of bacteriophage Mu Gam protein and Green Fluorescent Protein. Gam binds to DNA double-strand break ends, forming bright green fluorescent foci that mark DSB locations in real time.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: RecA Filaments
description: RecA protein polymerizes on single-stranded DNA at DSB sites, forming nucleoprotein filaments. These filaments catalyze homologous recombination for repair and also trigger the SOS response by stimulating LexA auto-cleavage.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: LexA Repressor
description: LexA is a transcriptional repressor that keeps SOS response genes silenced under normal conditions. When RecA filaments form at DSBs, they stimulate LexA to auto-cleave, derepressing ~40 SOS genes including DNA repair enzymes.

name: RecBCD Enzyme
description: A bacterial helicase-nuclease that processes broken DNA ends during homologous recombination repair. GamGFP competes with RecBCD by capping DNA ends first.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: Double-Strand Break (DSB)
description: A severe form of DNA damage where both strands of the double helix are severed. UV radiation and environmental toxins can induce DSBs directly or indirectly via replication fork collapse.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: Plasmid DNA
description: Small, extra-chromosomal circular DNA molecules used to express reporter constructs like GamGFP and TetR-mCherry in the Shee Lab's experimental system.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: Capsule
description: The outermost protective layer of the E. coli bacterium.

name: Cell Wall
description: A rigid layer of peptidoglycan that gives the bacterium its shape.

name: Plasma Membrane
description: A phospholipid bilayer controlling transport in and out of the cell.

name: Flagella
description: Helical appendages used for cellular locomotion.

name: Pili / Fimbriae
description: Fine hair-like appendages on the cell surface used for attachment.
